A '''right-handed coordinate system''' is an [[orthonormal basis]] used to model 3-dimensional [[Euclidean space]] with a particular direction convention.

[[File:Right-handed-coordinate-system.svg|300px|center]]

== Formal definition ==

Let $\mathbb{E}^3$ be a three dimensional [[Euclidean space]].

An orthonormal vector list $(\hat x, \hat y, \hat z)$ satisfying the following condition is a '''right-handed coordinate system''':

* Using a right human hand, point the index finger and the thumb in the direction of $\hat x,\hat z$ respectively,
* then the middle finger can point to the direction of $\hat y$.
